title: Keep useful job artifacts
summary: An artifact is a saved file from a job, such as a test report or built package. It lets later steps or reviewers inspect useful results.
introduction: An artifact is a saved file from a job, such as a test report or built package. It lets later steps or reviewers inspect useful results. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An artifact is a saved file from a job, such as a test report or built package. It lets later steps or reviewers inspect useful results.

blocks.code:
Job: accessibility checks
Artifact: accessibility-report.json
Purpose: inspect which pages passed or failed
Retention: keep only as long as the project needs
blocks.title: Keep useful job artifacts

blocks.text: The report adds evidence beyond a green or red status. An artifact may contain sensitive data, so choose its contents and access thoughtfully.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name one useful artifact from a screenshot comparison job.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not save secrets or private source data into broadly accessible artifacts.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
